newsitem.title: HONG KONG: People of HK give UK PM Blair ecstatic reception.
newsitem.headline: People of HK give UK PM Blair ecstatic reception.

text.p: Chanting "Tony, we love you", Hong Kong people on Monday gave visiting British Prime Minister Tony Blair a tumultuous reception as he walked through a city shopping mall hours before the colony's handover to China.
Thousands cheered, clapped and roared their approval of Blair as he went on a walkabout accompanied by Britain's 28th and last colonial Governor Chris Patten.

Crowds pushed forward to shake Blair's hand and grab a quick autograph as the prime minister, clearly moved by the ecstatic welcome, walked in Pacific Place, one of the shopping centres that has made Hong Kong a paradise for conspicuous consumption.

Blair, facing delirious crowds within just two hours of flying into Hong Kong for the end of 156 years of colonial rule, said: "It is amazing. People feel a great sense of affection. It is something we can be proud of."
"Tony, we love you," crowds chanted, and one onlooker shouted, "Good luck for the next five years" to the British Labour leader, who swept to a landslide election win on May 1.
Every time Blair paused to wave to the crowd, people roared their approval and hundreds of flash bulbs went off to record the emotion-charged moment.
Patten was also given a rousing reception by the people to whom he gave democratic reforms in the last five years of British rule, much to the rage of Beijing.
"Thank you so much. We will always be grateful," one Hong Kong Chinese said as he surged towards the crush barriers to shake Patten's hand.
Patten, who has had to wipe a tear from his eye at many emotional farewells, said he found it a very moving experience.
On arrival in Hong Kong, Blair offered a blunt message to China -- he was eager to build a strong and stable relationship but not at the expense of Hong Kong's freedoms.

Asked what message he would deliver in talks with China's President Jiang Zemin before the handover ceremony, Blair told reporters: "What is absolutely essential is that there are two pillars, foundations of our relationship for the future.
"The first is adherence to the joint declaration, the agreement between Britain and China that guarantees the future prosperity and freedom of Hong Kong.
"Second is our desire to build a strong and stable relationship with China for the future, which is both in the interests of the people of Hong Kong as well as the people of the United Kingdom."
Blair, underlying the historic date of his lightning visit, "This is obviously a momentous day for China, for Britain and most of all the people of Hong Kong.
"Hong Kong has become one of the most successful and prosperous parts of the world."
